title: AI security posture tools ship auto-remediation for AI packages by Q4 2026
body: Orca Security's 2026 State of AI Security report, summarized July 13, found that 99.9% of AI-related vulnerability alerts that already have a fix available remain unpatched, with 81.2% of AI-running organizations carrying at least one known vulnerability and 74.1% carrying at least one critical CVE — even as 56% of adopters have pushed agent frameworks and 64% have wired vector databases into production. The arresting number is not the presence of flaws but the fix-available-yet-untouched backlog: the patch exists and is simply not applied. Orca is itself an agentless cloud-security (CNAPP) vendor whose platform already automates prioritization and remediation for conventional cloud risk, so publishing this precise statistic doubles as a product-roadmap tell. I expect the detection-heavy AI security posture management (AI-SPM) market to answer the backlog on the remediation side: by Q4 2026 at least one major cloud- or security-posture vendor — Orca, Wiz, Palo Alto Networks Prisma Cloud, Microsoft Defender for Cloud, or a CNAPP peer — ships a named feature that does not merely flag AI-package and agent-framework CVEs but drives them down, through auto-prioritized patch workflows, one-click or auto-generated fixes, and a mean-time-to-remediate or patch-coverage metric scoped to AI assets. The forcing function is competitive and timed: the report lands the same week as working attacks on agent memory and immediately ahead of Black Hat, DEF CON's AI Village, and the August AI Risk Summit, where every posture vendor will want to convert '99.9% unpatched' from an indictment into a shipped answer. Detection alone now reads as restating the problem; the differentiated pitch is closing the fixable gap before agentic autonomy turns one unpatched flaw into a self-propagating incident.

reasoning.because: Orca's 2026 report finds 99.9% of fixable AI vulnerabilities remain unpatched
reasoning.given: CNAPP/AI-SPM tooling is detection-heavy as agent frameworks and vector DBs surge into production
reasoning.so_that: ≥1 major CNAPP/AI-SPM vendor ships auto-remediation that drives down the fixable AI-package CVE backlog
reasoning.landing: by Q4 2026; ≥1 major posture vendor ships a named AI-remediation feature
reasoning.plain_language: Almost every AI security hole that already has a fix sits unpatched, so security tools will start fixing them automatically, not just flagging them.

summary: Orca's 2026 AI-security report finds 99.9% of fixable AI vulnerabilities sit unpatched even as agent frameworks and vector databases reach production. By Q4 2026, at least one major cloud- or security-posture vendor likely ships auto-remediation that burns down the fixable AI-package backlog.
